observations: The material mask is vertically symmetric about the 2 um centerline.
There are five independent, full-length horizontal rails across the center gap.
Each half contains two connected fanout/meander-like components: an outer broad tapered body and an inner five-rail fanout with rounded/sloped side transitions.
The top and bottom halves terminate at the footprint edges in four broad vertical side leads per half; the central rails span the full 120 um footprint.
The two tiny isolated pixels in the lower half are treated as raster noise rather than device topology.
topology_reasoning.working_model: The recreation uses primitive straight/taper/rectangle assemblies for the five central rails, mirrored upper/lower broad bodies, and mirrored inner rail fanouts. The geometry is kept explicit and parametric so the rail pitch, guide width, fanout dimensions, body dimensions, and a representative arm length are real top-level knobs.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitive assembly; outer and inner leads were sloped paths and the lower copy used an incorrect mirror transform, producing a vertically oversized candidate.
Adjusted lead endpoints and attempted to correct the lower-half transform; the candidate bbox was still incorrect.
Switched the lower half to a 180 degree reference rotation about the 60 x 2 um center, fixing the reflection direction.
Replaced the broad sloped side paths with segmented primitive vertical tapers; this brought the device bbox close to 120 x 4 um and matched the main side mass.
Replaced the inner lead paths with three exact-endpoint taper segments per side and flattened only the written GDS assembly for the independent area check; retained as best.
